title: AI & Jobs
hook: AI is less likely to take your whole job than to take certain tasks within it. The pattern through history: tools reshape work faster than they erase it.
key_points: AI tends to automate specific tasks, not entire jobs all at once.
Routine, repetitive work is most exposed; judgment and people-skills less so.
New tools also create new roles and shift what 'the job' means.
The durable skill is learning to work *with* AI, not competing against it.
content_html: No question about AI causes more anxiety than "will it take my job?" The honest answer is more nuanced than the headlines. AI is very good at tasks — drafting text, summarizing documents, sorting information, generating first attempts — but a job is usually a bundle of many tasks, plus judgment, relationships, and accountability. So the common pattern isn't a profession vanishing overnight; it's parts of many jobs getting automated while the rest changes shape.
extra_html: History is a useful guide here. Spreadsheets didn't end accounting; they changed what accountants spend their time on and let them do more. ATMs didn't eliminate bank tellers as fast as people feared. New tools tend to reshape work — and create roles that didn't exist before — faster than they erase it. That said, the disruption is real and uneven: routine, repetitive, text-heavy work is more exposed, while jobs leaning on hands-on skill, human connection, and hard judgment are more sheltered. The most reliable response isn't to compete with AI on speed; it's to get comfortable using it, so the boring parts of your work get faster and your distinctly human contribution gets more room.

related.title: What AI Actually Is
related.hook: AI isn't a thinking robot — it's software that learns patterns from huge piles of examples, then uses them to make a good guess about something new.

related.title: Using AI Responsibly
related.hook: The point of AI literacy isn't to use AI for everything — it's to use it well: check its work, be honest that you used it, and know the moments to put it down.

flashcards.prompt: How does AI most commonly affect jobs?

choices.text: It automates specific tasks within a job rather than the whole job
It instantly eliminates entire professions overnight
It has no effect on how work is done

flashcards.explanation_html: AI usually absorbs particular tasks — drafting, summarizing, sorting — reshaping roles rather than wiping out whole occupations at once.

flashcards.prompt: What's the most durable career response to AI?
flashcards.back_html: Learn to work with it — use AI to handle routine tasks while you focus on judgment, creativity, and people — rather than competing head-on.
